newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian truckers to set strike date March 22.
newsitem.headline: Colombian truckers to set strike date March 22.

text.p: Colombia's main association of truck drivers will set a date for a national strike at a meeting on March 22, a senior member of the organization said on Tuesday.

The indefinite stoppage is being called to pressure the government and transport companies to fulfill the terms of a 19-point agreement drawn up last October. The pact ended a crippling 11-day strike by the Colombian Truckers' Association (ACC).

A fax sent to ACC members this week said: "In the meeting of the association's national directorate to be held March 22, we will definitely be setting the zero hour for the start of a new stoppage by all our members and affiliates at national level with the aim of demanding the fulfilment (of the earlier accord)."
National directorate member Mario Quiroga told Reuters the strike would probably start after Easter Sunday, March 30.
Quiroga said the ACC had a membership of 5,000 owner- operators and at least 180,000 drivers, representing about 80 percent of all Colombian truckers.

In its 11-day strike last October, the ACC stopped virtually all freight shipped by road and delayed the shipment of at least 250,000 60-kg bags of coffee exports, according to the National Coffee Growers' Federation.
The deal to resolve the October strike provided for an immediate 16 percent increase in freight rates, with a further 14 percent rise at the start of this year.
The accord also included provisions to cut the cost of highway tolls, operating licenses and associated taxes, as well as a pledge to review maximum load restrictions.
Quiroga said none of the 19 points in the agreement had taken effect.

"There has been a lack of seriousness on the part of the government. There has been a total lack of commitment. It's much more profitable for the transport companies and cargo owners than for us the truckers," Quiroga said.
